economy.summary: Jackson's campaign site says work should support a family in Franklin County and supports raising the state minimum wage from $7.25 to at least $14.50 per hour. He also proposes investing in resources to start and grow local businesses and supporting paid apprenticeships and work-based learning programs.
economy.short: Supports raising minimum wage to $14.50, local business investment, apprenticeships.

taxes.summary: Jackson's campaign site says government should live within its means, spending no more than projected tax and fee revenue. He supports childcare subsidies or income tax relief for childcare expenses.
taxes.short: Proposes spending within projected revenue; supports childcare tax relief.

education.summary: Jackson's campaign site proposes increased funding for local public education with a focus on recruiting and retaining teachers. He would also establish mandatory high school instruction in the U.S. Constitution, Bill of Rights, and constitutional amendments.
education.short: Supports increased public school funding, teacher retention, constitution instruction.

healthcare.summary: Jackson's campaign site says healthcare should be a right, not a privilege. He proposes expanding the Pennie program to offset lost ACA premium credits for low-wage earners, stopping the loss of healthcare services in Franklin County, and reducing healthcare costs.
healthcare.short: Supports expanding Pennie, reducing costs, retaining local healthcare services.

energy.summary: Jackson's campaign site supports clean, sustainable energy projects throughout Franklin County, along with land conservation, soil health improvements, and stream restoration. He proposes preventing farmland loss to warehouses and blocking AI data center construction.
energy.short: Supports clean energy, land conservation; proposes blocking data centers, warehouse sprawl.

economy.summary: Kauffman voted against House Bill 1500 in June 2023, which would have raised Pennsylvania's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 per hour by 2026 in annual steps. The bill passed the House 103-100.
economy.short: Voted against raising state minimum wage to $15 by 2026.

taxes.summary: In a February 2025 statement on the governor's budget address, Kauffman said the proposal spends well beyond the means of the state and that the state cannot continue spending more than it has. He said the proposed spending path would require raising taxes in future years, which he does not want to see happen.
taxes.short: Opposes governor's budget as overspending; opposes future tax increases.

abortion.summary: Kauffman voted against House Bill 1786 in November 2023, which would bar Pennsylvania courts and officers from assisting other states' civil and criminal cases involving reproductive health care services. The bill passed the House 117-86.
abortion.short: Voted against bill limiting other states' reproductive-health case cooperation.

education.summary: Kauffman voted against House Bill 2370 in June 2024, which would revise the state's basic education funding formula, add adequacy supplements for underfunded districts, and set a flat statewide cyber charter tuition rate. The bill passed the House 107-94.
education.short: Voted against revised school funding formula and cyber charter rate.

guns.summary: Kauffman voted against House Bill 1593 in September 2025, which would remove the state's background-check exemption for long guns and require background checks on sales and transfers of rifles and shotguns. The bill passed the House 104-99.
guns.short: Voted against background checks on rifle and shotgun sales.
